weather.tip: Overcast with rain odds at 100% through the evening — keep an umbrella handy for your commute home and pad your travel time on flood-prone stretches; it'll cool to near 19-20°C overnight.

around.headline: MTech student dies by suicide in IISc Bengaluru hostel room
around.summary: An MTech student at IISc Bengaluru died by suicide in his hostel room, according to today's reports, and police are investigating the circumstances. If you or someone you know is struggling, Karnataka's Tele-MANAS helpline (1800-599-0019) offers free, confidential counselling 24/7.
around.source: The New Indian Express, Deccan Herald

around.headline: Tanker driver arrested after nearly running over biker in Bengaluru's Varthur
around.summary: A water tanker driver was arrested in Varthur after nearly running over a two-wheeler rider, an incident caught on video, per today's report. Give tankers and trucks a wide berth at junctions and while overtaking — their blind spots make bikers riding alongside easy to miss.

around.headline: Bengaluru airport departure fee cut 33%, but a new arrival charge starts September 1
around.summary: AERA has cut Bengaluru airport's user fee to Rs 300 for domestic and Rs 997 for international departures, even as KIA begins levying a separate User Development Fee on arriving passengers from September 1, per today's reports. If you're flying out soon your departure just got a little cheaper, but budget extra for your next incoming flight.
around.source: The Hindu, The Times of India

around.headline: Nearly 70% of Bengaluru's white-topping road projects miss deadlines
around.summary: Close to 70% of the city's white-topping road projects have blown past their deadlines, leaving commuters to navigate prolonged dug-up stretches, per today's report. If your daily route runs through an active white-topping site, expect the disruption to outlast the original timeline and keep a backup road in mind.

around.headline: Karnataka bans sale of analogue, non-dairy paneer sold as "paneer" for one year
around.summary: Karnataka's FDA has imposed a one-year ban on selling analogue or synthetic paneer under the paneer label, citing public health concerns over adulteration, per today's report. When buying loose paneer or eating out, it's worth asking whether it's genuine dairy paneer now that enforcement has tightened.

around.headline: US imposes 50% tariffs on $20 billion of Canadian goods after trade talks collapse
around.summary: The US has imposed 50% tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian goods after negotiations broke down, per today's report. Trade shocks like this tend to ripple into commodity and currency markets, so it's worth watching if you hold export-linked investments or have major dollar purchases planned soon.

events.note: Traditional Onam feast happening in Bengaluru — book ahead if you want a table.

events.name: Book Brahma Literature Festival
events.note: Still running in Bengaluru with talks on language and literature — check the day's lineup before heading out.

events.note: A month-long theatre festival marking the veteran theatre director's birth anniversary.

events.note: Its biggest handmade-craft edition yet, with artisans from across India — a good stop for festive shopping.

events.note: An India-Italy art exhibition exploring the theme of motherhood — worth a visit if you're near Palace Road.

street_smart.title: You get a call from someone identifying himself as a "Cognizant data security officer," citing today's news that Cognizant confirmed a data breach and is offering affected individuals $1 million in identity-theft cover. He already knows your name, employee ID, and that you worked with Cognizant, and offers to "activate" your free protection right now — he just needs to verify your PAN, Aadhaar, and an OTP about to hit your phone. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Today's real story: Cognizant confirmed a data breach and is offering affected individuals $1 million in identity-theft cover (The Times of India). Cognizant only appeared as a plain news item in this morning's brief, not yet as a street-smart scenario — this applies a fresh angle: the post-breach vishing call that typically follows such disclosures.
street_smart.situation: He sounds professional, already has accurate personal details, and says the identity-theft enrollment window closes today if you don't verify now.

choices.text: Hang up, and separately go to Cognizant's official breach-notification email or website to enroll in the free identity-theft protection yourself — never share your PAN, Aadhaar, or OTP with an inbound caller.
choices.feedback: Correct — the breach itself is real, but Cognizant's own enrollment never requires reading an OTP over a phone call. The caller's accurate details just mean the breach handed him that information too; it isn't proof he's genuine staff.

choices.text: Since he already knows so much accurate detail, share the OTP and PAN so he can "activate" the cover before the window closes.
choices.feedback: This is the trap — the caller's accuracy came from the very breach he's citing, not from being genuine Cognizant staff. Reading an OTP aloud hands over live account access; no legitimate identity-protection enrollment ever needs that.

choices.text: Ask for his employee ID and a callback number, hang up, then call that number back before sharing anything.
choices.feedback: Better instinct, but the callback number he gives you can just as easily be a second line the same scam ring controls. Only a number you find independently — from Cognizant's official site or the breach email — is safe to call.

choices.text: Refuse to share the OTP, but give your PAN since it's already on your Aadhaar card anyway.
choices.feedback: PAN alone can't drain an account, but combined with other data from the breach it helps a scammer impersonate you elsewhere — for loans, SIM swaps, or KYC fraud. Treat it as sensitive even when a caller already seems to "know everything."

takeaways: A real breach notification doesn't make an inbound caller safe to trust — always re-verify using the phone number or portal from the company's official site or email, never one the caller supplies.
No legitimate identity-theft enrollment or bank process ever needs you to read an OTP aloud over a call — that request alone is the giveaway.
After any breach involving your employer or bank, expect a spike in calls or SMS citing it by name for weeks afterward — scammers buy leaked data and work through it in batches.

quiz.question: What is Bengaluru airport's new domestic passenger user fee after AERA's revision, per today's report?
quiz.why: The international departure fee was set at Rs 997 — both cuts are part of AERA's new passenger-friendly tariff formula.

quiz.question: Which Karnataka body's chief is the state cabinet renewing its push to suspend, after a high court setback?
quiz.why: The Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) conducts the state's civil service recruitment exams.

quiz.question: The US recently imposed 50% tariffs on $20 billion worth of goods from which country, after trade talks collapsed?
quiz.why: The tariffs followed a breakdown in trade negotiations between the two countries, per today's report.

quiz.question: In which Karnataka district does the Cauvery river originate, at Talakaveri?
quiz.why: Talakaveri, on the Brahmagiri hills in Kodagu, is both the river's source and a revered pilgrimage site.

quiz.question: What is the term for the interest rate at which the RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks?
quiz.why: The reverse repo rate is the opposite — the rate the RBI pays banks to park their surplus funds with it.
